external_source_refresh.finding: Activation Addition modifies intermediate activations during inference using activation-difference steering vectors, so a genuine Trigger-1 success must evidence an internal consumed intervention rather than prompt text alone.
Contrastive Activation Addition applies positive or negative coefficients to residual-stream steering vectors, supporting signed directionality controls.

Per-instance activation-steering results published 2026-08-09 report that useful intervention layers vary by input and that over-steering can degrade outputs; calibration must therefore remain separate from holdout evaluation.
Current llama.cpp exposes control-vector generation and runtime application with --control-vector-scaled and --control-vector-layer-range, including CPU-only generation examples.
Current llama.cpp source validates control-vector embedding width against model n_embd and copies layer-major float data into per-layer control tensors before applying the selected layer range.
TransformerLens current supported-model list includes Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-Base, preserving Qwen3-0.6B as a low-friction instrumentation baseline.

Qwen3.5-0.8B currently exposes hidden_size=1024, num_hidden_layers=24 and a repeating three linear-attention plus one full-attention layer pattern, so model-specific adapter identity must include layer type as well as layer index.
